restoration_note: Teaching 57 unfolds a sustained correspondential parable: the body as a city of inner storehouses, with each of the five senses (eyes, ears, nose, tongue, hands) operating as an enthumesis — a faculty that gathers impressions outside, carries them inward to its storehouse, watches over them, and produces them on demand for whoever asks. The heart's enthumesis rules over all five as king and steward. The body itself is then re-described as an encampment with gates and watchmen, where what is fellow-citizen with the self passes freely but what is foreign is hindered — until the Mind of Light comes, humbles the guard-archons, and takes the keys. Restoration was tightly constrained by the parallel structure: the same formulaic clauses recur five or six times (ϣⲁⲥⲝⲓⲧⲥ̄ ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ ⲁⲛⲉⲥⲧⲁⲙⲓⲟⲛ, ⲡⲣⲉϩϣⲓⲛⲉ ⲉⲧϣⲓⲛⲉ ⲙ̄ⲙⲁⲥ, Ⲧ̄ϩⲉ ⲁⲛ ⲧⲉ ⲧⲉⲓ̈, etc.), so most one- and two-letter gaps and many medium gaps were recoverable with high confidence. Three whole-line lacunae (3506–3508) and the worst-damaged stretches in the touch-section and the cellarer simile resisted reliable fill and were marked unrestorable. The vocabulary throughout is the standard storehouse/gate/watchman lexicon already established in the corpus: ⲧⲁⲙⲓⲟⲛ, ⲁⲡⲟⲑⲏⲕⲏ, ⲣⲱⲟⲩ, ⲍⲟⲩⲣⲉⲧⲉ, ⲡⲣⲉϩϣⲓⲛⲉ, ⲡⲣ̄ⲡⲙⲉⲩⲉ, ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲥ ⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲛⲉ.
